instruction: You are given `/home/user/Desktop/fatigue_base.fst`, `/home/user/Desktop/turbsim_fatigue_base.inp`, `/home/user/Desktop/inflow_fatigue.dat`, and their version-matched dependencies. Complete a fatigue DEL workflow from the command line: 1. Copy the TurbSim template to `fatigue_wind.inp`, retaining the supplied official seeds (`13428`, `RanLux`), 31x31 grid, `dt=0.05 s`, IEC class B, `AnalysisTime=630 s`, and `UsableTime=ALL`; confirm `HubHt=RefHt=90 m` and `URef=11.4 m/s`. Run TurbSim to generate `fatigue_wind.bts`. 2. Run `fatigue.fst` for 600 s with InflowWind `WindType=3` pointing to that BTS and retain the complete text `fatigue.out` plus normal-termination logs. 3. Write `/home/user/Desktop/fatigue_post.py`. Discard samples with `Time<60 s`. For `RootMyb1` and `TwrBsMyt`, remove consecutive duplicates, retain endpoints and local reversals, and apply ASTM E1049 four-point rainflow counting: count closed cycles as 1.0 and every residual range as a 0.5 half cycle. Use full peak-to-valley ranges `S_i`, not amplitudes. Save every range, mean, count, and endpoints to `/home/user/Desktop/cycles.csv`. 4. Compute `DEL=(sum(n_i*S_i^m)/1e6)^(1/m)` with `m=10` for `RootMyb1` and `m=4` for `TwrBsMyt`. Both source channels are kN-m; divide only the final tower DEL by 1000 to report MN-m. 5. Save `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` as `rootmyb1_del_knm, twrbsmyt_del_mnm`. 6. Do not use GUI tools. [Init Package Note] Only initialization inputs are preloaded; generate all wind, simulation, cycle, and summary artifacts yourself.
